answer: Zero-knowledge national-ID binding: one person, one agent. An agent proves it holds a government credential with a zero-knowledge proof, revealing only a unique nullifier. The registry stores only the nullifier. Reusing that credential yields the same nullifier and instant rejection. Revocation lists are checked against issuers each epoch. Forging 1,000 sybils needs 1,000 real identities: stolen IDs sell for about $50 each, so $50,000, plus arrest risk. Like a grove where each tree carries one beacon, and an island that lets only one boat land per lighthouse flash.
